CDU.name: Crude Distillation Unit
CDU.description: Primary fractional distillation column operating at atmospheric pressure to separate crude oil into fractions based on boiling points.
CDU.purpose: To separate crude oil into component fractions using boiling point differences under atmospheric pressure.
facts: Separates crude oil fractions based on boiling points under atmospheric pressure.
Produces Light Naphtha, Heavy Naphtha, Kerosene, Light Gas Oil (Atmospheric Gas Oil), and Atmospheric Residue.
Atmospheric residue serves as the primary feedstock for the Vacuum Distillation Unit (VDU).

VDU.name: Vacuum Distillation Unit
VDU.description: Fractional distillation unit operating under deep vacuum to separate heavy atmospheric residue from the CDU into lighter gas oils and vacuum residue without thermal cracking.
VDU.purpose: To separate heavy distillation residues at lower temperatures under vacuum to prevent thermal cracking.
facts: Operates under vacuum (typically 0.5 to 1.5 psi absolute) to reduce boiling points of heavy hydrocarbons.
Separates Atmospheric Residue into Light Vacuum Gas Oil (LVGO), Heavy Vacuum Gas Oil (HVGO), and Vacuum Residue.
Prevents thermal cracking of heavy hydrocarbons which occurs at temperatures above 800°F (427°C).

FCC.name: Fluid Catalytic Cracking Unit
FCC.description: Conversion unit using fluidized zeolite catalyst at high temperature to crack heavy vacuum gas oils into lighter high-value products like high-octane gasoline, light cycle oil, and LPG.
FCC.purpose: To crack heavy gas oils into high-value transportation fuels (gasoline, LPG) using a fluidized catalyst.
facts: Uses a circulating fluidized bed of zeolite catalyst at high temperatures (950°F to 1050°F).
Cracks long-chain vacuum gas oils (VGO) into lighter products like high-octane gasoline, diesel/light cycle oil (LCO), and LPG.
Does NOT extract aromatics from heavy fuel oil; it is a catalytic cracking conversion process.
Catalyst deactivation is primarily caused by coke deposition (reversible via regeneration) and metal poisoning (nickel, vanadium, iron; irreversible).

Hydrotreater.name: Hydrotreater Unit (Hydrodesulfurization)
Hydrotreater.description: Catalytic purification process that reacts petroleum fractions with hydrogen at elevated temperature and pressure to remove sulfur, nitrogen, and metals, and saturate olefins.
Hydrotreater.purpose: To remove sulfur, nitrogen, metals, and other impurities from feedstocks to meet environmental standards and protect downstream catalysts.
facts: Reacts hydrocarbon feedstocks with hydrogen in the presence of a metal catalyst (e.g., CoMo or NiMo on alumina).
Removes sulfur (hydrodesulfurization), nitrogen (hydrodenitrogenation), and trace metals, and saturates olefins.
Does NOT remove water from crude oil (that is done by the desalter in/before the CDU).
Protects downstream reforming and isomerization catalysts from poisoning (e.g., protecting reformer platinum catalysts).

Storage Terminal.name: Storage Terminal / Tank Farm
Storage Terminal.description: Logistics and inventory buffer system consisting of storage tanks to receive, hold, blend, and distribute crude feedstocks and finished refinery products.
products: Finished fuels (Gasoline, Diesel, Jet Fuel, Heating Oil)
Storage Terminal.purpose: To manage feedstock inventory, provide blending capacity, buffer unit imbalances, and store finished fuels prior to pipeline, rail, barge, or truck distribution.
facts: Manages inventory buffers between incoming crude supply and refinery process units.
Provides storage and blending facilities for finished fuels to meet commercial specifications (e.g., octane blending, vapor pressure).
Ensures continuous operation by decoupling production units from immediate logistics delays.

Catalyst Deactivation.name: Catalyst Deactivation
Catalyst Deactivation.description: Loss of catalytic activity and/or selectivity over time due to chemical, thermal, or mechanical mechanisms.
facts: Coking: Deposition of carbonaceous residue (coke) on catalyst active sites (reversible via regenerator burning).
Poisoning: Irreversible chemical bonding of impurities (heavy metals like nickel, vanadium, sodium, iron; or sulfur/nitrogen on reforming catalysts) to active sites.
Sintering: Thermal degradation and loss of active surface area due to exposure to high temperatures.
Fouling/Plugging: Physical blockage of catalyst pores or bed by particulates or polymer formation.
